newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee eases mildly on dlr demand from north.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee eases mildly on dlr demand from north.

text.p: The rupee eased mildly against the dollar on Thursday following demand for the U.S. currency from New Delhi-based banks, dealers said.
"There are deals at 35.71, but not beyond," said a dealer.
The rupee had opened Thursday unchanged at 35.700/705 against the dollar. Dealers said dollar purchases from Delhi appeared to be a one-off deal and did not portend a trend.
But some dealers saw it as a sign of month-end surge in dollar demand.
Forward dollar premiums opened slightly lower but dealers attributed this to weekend factors. The forward market was otherwise largely dull, they said.
